items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: This expansion happened because of this incredible woman we met and who we have renamed St. Agnes.

ctx.x: That program has expanded greatly over the years, I gather.

Well, that’s because of the person I was just going to talk about, who is someone we’ve renamed Saint Agnes Varis. This expansion happened because of this incredible woman we met and who we have renamed St. Agnes. It’s Agnes Varis who was so wonderful to the Metropolitan Opera and to Jazz at Lincoln Center. We met Agnes... I invited her to one of our moments... Shortly after Katrina, Dick Parsons, who I also want to shout out to, became our Chairman. I knew he was on too many boards, so I asked him if he could…
What a logistical feat, to implement that program on that scope.

items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: She was just like my mom. She was the person who ended up giving me in advice in life that I never really... She was quite incredible. She affected me greatly.

ctx.x: That’s one of your many programs. That’s the Jazz in the Schools program.
The Agnes Varis Jazz & Blues in the Schools program.
